reason: The hypothesis makes several specific claims about the oxidation behavior and failure mechanisms of this particular high-entropy alloy, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these key premises. The claims are presented without reference to experimental data or literature on this or similar alloy systems.
premises: Additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 forms a protective Al/Cr-rich oxide scale under moderately oxidizing conditions.
Reducing or excessively oxidative conditions disrupt the formation or adherence of this protective scale.
A compromised oxide scale leads to internal oxidation and element depletion in the alloy.
Internal oxidation and element depletion increase intergranular stresses.
Increased intergranular stresses facilitate crack initiation and propagation, leading to catastrophic failure.
